paragraphs.source_en: The animal-like rock is just at the entrance to the narrow wadi and it is visible from outside. Could similar phenomena explain why in the Tassili certain sites were chosen for image-making whereas others were ignored? Among a large number of sites the presence of unusual formations could have attracted the attention of prehistoric groups and the locality would then become a special one. Thus, the narrow wadi of In Itinen en haut might have been a sacred area guarded by the "animal" at the entrance. The kind of paintings depicted suggests that this place was used for special events and its restricted space meant that only a limited number of people could have entered at a time. The exceptional status of the wadi and the intention to paint exclusively in this delimited space of the site is supported by the fact that there are no Round Head paintings immediately outside this area.

paragraphs.source_en: The two sites, although both located on the Tassili Plateau, present some fundamental differences in the topography but at the same time they show similarities in the typology of some paintings, their repainting and their delimitation by stone structures. The paintings at Tin Aboteka are exposed and visible from a great distance, whereas the paintings at In Itinen en haut are situated in a small hidden wadi. The different morphology of the two sites shows that they may have been used for different purposes. A large community could have easily stayed in the open site of Tin Aboteka, but at In Itinen en haut only a few groups could have entered at a time.

paragraphs.source_en: The possible function of a single shelter can be hypothesized according to its location in the landscape and the paintings represented. If the images were part of cults or rituals, they were located in shelters designated for such purposes and for this reason the interpretation is only possible considering both the place and the images. The ethnographic record shows that one of the most common uses of shelters is for initiation rites requiring hidden places for the preparation of young boys or girls.
